description: Fee records whose maker rebate rate equals 0.0005 exactly are included along with those above it.

b.request: For fee records where `rebrate >= 0.0005`, return one row containing `SUM(rebtotal)` and `AVG(feerate - rebrate)`, in that order, unrounded; ignore NULL values in each aggregate and return NULL for an aggregate with no values.
b.sql: SELECT SUM(rebtotal), AVG(feerate - rebrate) FROM fees WHERE rebrate >= 0.0005
b.raw: For fee records where `rebrate >= 0.0005`, return one row containing `SUM(rebtotal)` and `AVG(feerate - rebrate)`, in that order, unrounded; ignore NULL values in each aggregate and return NULL for an aggregate with no values.

a.request: Across all fee records whose maker rebate rate (`rebrate`) is at least 0.0005, what are the total rebate (the sum of `rebtotal`) and the average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`)? Return one row with these two values in that order, unrounded, ignoring missing values (each value is empty if there is nothing to aggregate).
a.sql: SELECT SUM(rebtotal) AS total_rebate, AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS average_net_fee_rate FROM fees WHERE rebrate >= 0.0005

d.request: For fee records with `rebrate >= 0.0005`, return one row containing `SUM(rebtotal)` and `AVG(feerate - rebrate)`, in that order, unrounded, with missing values ignored and each aggregate empty if it has no values.
d.sql: SELECT SUM(rebtotal), AVG(feerate - rebrate) FROM fees WHERE rebrate >= 0.0005

c.request: For the high-rebate fee records, using 0.0005 on the maker rebate rate (`rebrate`) as the cutoff, what are the total rebate (the sum of `rebtotal`) and the average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`)? Return one row with these two values in that order, unrounded, ignoring missing values (each value is empty if there is nothing to aggregate). Fee records whose maker rebate rate equals 0.0005 exactly are included along with those above it.
c.sql: SELECT SUM(rebtotal) AS total_rebate, AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS average_net_fee_rate FROM fees WHERE rebrate >= 0.0005
